# `silk/platform/native/report`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Writes the report of an unhandled error or a trap to a descriptor, with fixed limits.

## When to use
The native runtime (`silk.platform.native.start` and `silk.platform.native.diagnostics`) uses [`NativeReport`](#NativeReport) to
print an unhandled error and its call path to standard error. Use it in a custom runtime.

## Details
A report is lines of text:
```text
unhandled error: app.ConfigError
  at app/main.silk:12:5
  at app.load
```
Each fragment is written only if it fits in the byte limit. When a limit is reached, the report
is incomplete, and later calls write nothing. It does not allocate.

## Gotchas
- The report does not close the descriptor.
- A write can fail after part of a fragment was written.
- A report does not stop a trap or run cleanup.

## Examples
### Report an error to standard error
```silk
import silk.platform.native.report { NativeReport }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  // Write to standard error, with at most 512 bytes and 4 caller frames.
  let mut report = NativeReport.make(2, 512, 4)

  // Each call returns false if the report is incomplete.
  let head = run report.unhandled("app.ConfigError", "app/main.silk:12:5")
  let load = run report.frame("app.load")
  let start = run report.frame("app.main")
  if !head || !load || !start || !report.succeeded() {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `NativeReport` with `import silk.platform.native.report { NativeReport }`.

## `NativeReport`

```silk
pub struct NativeReport
```

One report: its descriptor, its remaining byte and frame limits, and whether it is complete.

### When to use
The native runtime (`silk.platform.native.start` and `silk.platform.native.diagnostics`) uses it to print an
unhandled error and its call path to standard error. Use it in a custom runtime.

### Details
Each fragment is written only if it fits in the byte limit. When a limit is reached, the

- A write can fail after part of a fragment was written.

<a id="NativeReport.impl.make"></a>

### Associated function `make`

```silk
pub fn make(fd: i32, byteLimit: usize, frameLimit: usize) -> NativeReport
```

Returns a report that writes to `fd`, with at most `byteLimit` bytes and `frameLimit` caller
frames. It does not allocate.

<a id="NativeReport.impl.indented"></a>

### Associated function `indented`

```silk
pub fn indented(fd: i32, byteLimit: usize, frameLimit: usize, indent: string<'static>) -> NativeReport
```

Returns a report like [`NativeReport.make`](#NativeReport.impl.make) that starts each line with `indent`. The
indent counts toward the byte limit.

#### When to use
Use it to nest a report under other output, such as a failed test under the test's name.

<a id="NativeReport.impl.restart"></a>

### Method `restart`

```silk
pub fn restart(self: &mut Self) -> ()
```

Starts a new report on the same descriptor, with the full byte and frame limits again.

#### When to use
Use it when one report writer serves several reports, such as one for each failed test.

<a id="NativeReport.impl.resume"></a>

### Method `resume`

```silk
pub fn resume(self: &mut Self) -> ()
```

Starts the next part of the same report with the full frame limit again. The byte limit
keeps counting, so a report that ran out of bytes stays incomplete.

#### When to use
Use it when one report has two lists of frames, such as a trap's caller frames and then the
cause the trap happened while handling.

<a id="NativeReport.impl.unhandled"></a>

### Method `unhandled`

```silk
pub effect fn unhandled(self: &mut Self, identity: string, source: string) -> bool
```

Writes `unhandled error: ` with `identity`, then the line ` at ` with `source`. Returns
false if the report is incomplete.

Call it after the runtime has dropped the error value.

<a id="NativeReport.impl.fatal"></a>

### Method `fatal`

```silk
pub effect fn fatal(self: &mut Self, reason: string, source: string) -> bool
```

Writes `fatal trap: ` with `reason`, then the line ` at ` with `source`. Returns false if
the report is incomplete.

<a id="NativeReport.impl.frame"></a>

### Method `frame`

```silk
pub effect fn frame(self: &mut Self, label: string) -> bool
```

Writes the line ` at ` with the caller `label`. Returns false if the report is incomplete.

When the frame limit is reached, it writes ` [trace truncated]` one time, and the report
becomes incomplete.

<a id="NativeReport.impl.truncate"></a>

### Method `truncate`

```silk
pub effect fn truncate(self: &mut Self) -> bool
```

Writes ` [trace truncated]`, and makes the report incomplete. Later calls write nothing. It
returns false.

<a id="NativeReport.impl.cause"></a>

### Method `cause`

```silk
pub effect fn cause(self: &mut Self, identity: string, source: string) -> bool
```

Writes `while handling: ` with `identity`, then the line ` at ` with `source`. Use it for an
earlier error that a handler was handling.

<a id="NativeReport.impl.succeeded"></a>

```silk
pub fn succeeded(self: &Self) -> bool
```

Returns whether all fragments were written within the limits.
